summary: The D-122 draft survives every attack the dispatch names and four I added. The subject is unmoved at baeea882... and mode 0444 at both start and end, and I edited nothing but this verdict, having written a stub first. All five cited pins reproduce byte-exactly at the draft's measurement: the v1 subject, both v1 verdicts (Claude 2 ACCEPT with blockers [] and shouldFix []; Codex ACCEPT with all three counts 0; each 0444, each on registerRow DR-116), COORD at ac10b3f9..., and file 08 at 1cdcf9d4.... The Claude 2 advisory array holds exactly four entries, TPP-C2-A1 through A4, and the draft records all four by ID without promoting any to SHOULD-FIX. The register claims hold: DR-116's single row at line 298 carries the token OPEN and matches the contract's domain, D-002 line 440 records 'no third-party support policy needed yet' as an explicit deferral, DR-122 is the SARIF row recorded at D-115, and condition 2 is 4 of 30 SATISFIED with condition 5 structurally last and NOT MET, so the readiness effect really is zero. The one thing that looked like a MUST-FIX was COORD carrying D-121 as ADOPTED while the draft calls it in-review. I traced provenance instead of charging it: COORD reconstructed at e4fd117 — the draft's own pin — contains no D-121 section at all and ends its recording series at D-120, so the draft was accurate when written; D-121 landed as commit 1d24e52 during this review, growing COORD by 2694 bytes that are a proven exact byte-prefix append of that single unrelated section, with all five gate artifacts unmoved. That is PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT, so neither it nor the consequent staleness is chargeable. Nothing SATISFIES, QUALIFIES, mints a D-096 (A) grant, edits file 08, supersedes the sibling D-096 deferral candidate, or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/. 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX: CONSENT.
